parole.significato: Suffix creating abstract nouns from nouns or adjectives
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـی (-i), from Persian ـی.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نامه (nâme), from Persian نامه (nâme, “letter”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـواری, from Persian ـواری (-vâri, “-like, -ish”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ـزاده (-zade), from Old Anatolian Turkish ـزاده (-zāde), from Persian ـزاده (-zâda). From zade. Cognate with Azerbaijani -zadə.

parole.significato: abdest (the Islamic act of washing parts of the body using water for ritual prayers and for handling and reading the Qu…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آبدست (âbdest), from Persian آبدست (âbdast), a compound of آب (âb, “water”) and دست (dast, “hand”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آفرین (āferīn, “well done”), from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (āferīn, “well done”), from Persian آفرین (âfarin, “bravo”), from Middle Persian 𐭠𐭯𐭥𐭩𐭭 (āfrīn, “praise, blessing”)
From Ottoman Turkish افسون (afsun), from Persian افسون (afsun).
From Ottoman Turkish آغوش (aguş), from Persian آغوش (âġuš).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عالی جناب (ʿâlî cenâb), derived from Persian عَالِیجَنَاب (âlîjanâb). By surface analysis, ali + cenap.

parole.significato: azarole, Mediterranean medlar (Crataegus monogyna); also, its fruit.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish آلوج (aluç), borrowed from Persian آلوچه (âluča), diminutive of آلو (âlu, “plum”).
From Ottoman Turkish آماده (amade, “ready, prepared”), from Persian آماده (âmâde).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آن بآن, from Persian [Term?], from Arabic آن (ʔān).
From Ottoman Turkish آستار (astar), from Persian آستر (âstar).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آواره (“exiled; vagrant; homeless; wretched; idle”), from Persian آواره (âvâre).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آزار (azar, “a reprimand, reproach, scolding”), from Persian آزار (âzâr), from Persian آزردن (âzordan, “to annoy, to torment”). Cognates with Azerbaijani azar, Northern Kurdish azar, Turkmen azar, Uzbek ozor, Zazaki azar.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish باجه (baca), borrowed from Persian باجه (bāja).
From Ottoman Turkish ﺑﺨﺘﻴﺎﺭ, from Persian بختیار (baxtiâr), compound of baht + yâr.
From Ottoman Turkish بالاپرواز (balapervaz), from Persian [Term?]. Equivalent to balâ + pervaz.

parole.significato: shingle, a thin board used as a covering for the roof
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بالار (balar, “joist, rafter”), from Persian [Term?].

parole.significato: some; an unspecified quantity or number of.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish بعضی (ba'zı), from Persian بعضی (ba'zi), from Arabic بَعْض (baʕḍ).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish باغشلامق (bağışlamak), from Old Anatolian Turkish باغشلامق (bağışlamak), from Persian بخش (baxš) (modern Turkish bağış via back-formation) + ـلا (-la) (whence -la). Akin to Karakhanid [Term?].
From Ottoman Turkish بداوا (bedava), from Persian باد آورد (bâd-âvard), from باد (bâd, “wind”) and آورد (âvard, “borne”).
From Ottoman Turkish بل (bel, “spade”), variant of بیل (bil), from Persian بیل (bil, “spade”).
From Ottoman Turkish بلكه (belki), from Persian بلکه (balke).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish برباد (berbād), from Persian برباد دادَن (bar-bâd dâdan, “to destroy, to ruin”, literally “to cast it into the wind”).
From Ottoman Turkish برهوا (berhava), from Persian.
From Persian برکمال (bar-kamâl), from بر (bar) + کمال (kamâl)
From Ottoman Turkish بر طرف (ber taraf), from Persian بر (bar) and Arabic طَرَف (ṭaraf).

parole.significato: horse (often derogatory denoting a useless or an old horse)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish بیگیر (beygir), from Persian بارگیر (bârgir, “beast of burden”), from بار (bâr, “load, burden, cargo”) + گیر (gir, “carrying”).
From Persian بیهوده (bihude, “ineffective, useless, futile, pointless, trivial”).
From Ottoman Turkish بی بی (bîbî), from Persian بیبی (bi-bi).

parole.significato: A fermented drink made from wheat or millet, bosa.
parole.testo: One of two possibilities: * inherited from Ottoman Turkish بوزه, from Persian بوزه (buze). * Possibly from bozmak ("to blemish, to blight, to spoil or ruin") and Ottoman Turkish بوز (boz) ("Gray, Brown" - referring to the color of the beverage).
From Ottoman Turkish بوسه (buse), from Persian بوسه (buse, “kiss”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جافجاف (cafcaf), from Persian [Term?].
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جنكاور (cengâver), from Persian جنگاور.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جراحی, from Persian جراحی (jarrâhi). By surface analysis, cerrah (“surgeon”) + -i (Persian abstract suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جمری (cimri), from Persian جمری (jamri).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جو جوك, from Persian جوجک, ultimately from childish talk. Compare Turkish cüce.
From Ottoman Turkish ﺩﺍﺩﻯ (dadı), from Persian دادا (dâdâ).
From Ottoman Turkish دار آغاجی (dar ağacı), from Persian دار (dâr) and Ottoman Turkish آغاج (ağac). Equivalent to dar + ağaç.
From Ottoman Turkish دارو (daru), from Persian دارو (dâru).

parole.significato: To put a mark on an animal's hide with a hot iron rod; to brand.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish داغلامق (daġlamaḳ, “to brand, to cauterize, to wound one's feelings”), from Ottoman Turkish داغ (daġ, “a brand made with a hot iron or a branding iron”), from Persian داغ (“sear, mark left by cauterization”), morphologically dağ + -la + -mak.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دم (dem), from Persian دم (dam).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دربدر (derbader, “vagrant, beggar”), from Persian در بدر (dar ba-dar, “from door to door”).
From Ottoman Turkish دربند (derbend), borrowed from Persian دربند (darband, literally “bar of a door, bolt; a barrier”), from در (dar, “door, gate, passage”) + بند (band, “band, tie, fastening”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دركاه (dergâh), from Persian درگاه (dargâh). By surface analysis, der + -gâh.

parole.significato: dervish, an itinerant Sufi mystic practicing voluntary poverty in devotion to God
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish درویش (derviş), from Persian درویش (darviš), from Middle Persian dlgwš (driyōš, “poor, needy”).
From Ottoman Turkish داستان (dastan), from Persian داستان (dâstân).
From Ottoman Turkish دستار (destar), from Persian دستار (dastâr, “turban”).
From Persian دیو (dēw) + آسا (âsâ).

parole.significato: gold or silver embroidery on velvet padded by cardboard
parole.testo: From Persian [Term?].
From Ottoman Turkish طوت (tut, dut), from Persian توت (tut).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دوشش, from Persian دو (dū, “two”) + شش (šaš, “six”).
Perhaps from Persian دزد.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ازبر (ezber), from Persian از بر (az bar, “by heart”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ازبرلمك (ezberlemek), from Persian از بر (az bar, “by heart”). Equivalent to ezber + -le.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فرشته (ferişteh, “angel”) (whence also ferişte, of the same meaning), from Persian فرشته (farišta, ferešte, “angel”). The unetymological final -h is due to the many other words of Persian origin ending in the sound.

parole.significato: An imperial title for Turkish, Mongolian and Tatar khans meaning "ruler of rulers.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خاقان (hakan), from Persian خاقان (xâqân), itself from Proto-Turkic *kagan. Doublet of kağan and han.
Derived from Persian خام (xâm).
Derived from Persian خم (xam).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خامور (hamur), from Persian خمیر (xamir), from Arabic خَمِير (ḵamīr).
From Ottoman Turkish خان (han), from Persian خان (xân, “caravanserai”).

From Ottoman Turkish خارق العاده, from Persian خارقالعاده (xâreqo-l-'âde), from Arabic خَارِقُ العَادَة (ḵāriqu al-ʕāda), equivalent to harika + adet. Compare Azerbaijani xariqüladə, Crimean Tatar harikulade and Uzbek xoriqulodda.
From Ottoman Turkish خصمانه (hasmane), from Persian خصمانه (xasmâne), from Arabic خَصْم (ḵaṣm).
From Ottoman Turkish خسته (hasta), from Old Anatolian Turkish خسته (ḫeste), from Persian خسته (xaste).

parole.significato: mortar (container used for pounding and grinding ingredients)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish هاون, from Persian هاون (hâvan).
From Ottoman Turkish خاویار (havyar), from Persian خاویار (xâvyâr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خزینهدار, from Persian خزینهدار. By surface analysis, hazine + -dar.
From Ottoman Turkish هله (hele), from Persian هله (hala, “pay attention!”).
Univerbation of hemzemin (“on the same level”) from Persian همزمین (ham-zamin) + geçit (“passageway”).
From Ottoman Turkish هر, from Persian هر (har). Cognate with Bengali হর (hor, “every”), Latin salvus (“safe, whole”), Ancient Greek ὅλος (hólos, “complete, whole”). Doublet of salvo.

From Ottoman Turkish هر شی, from now dated Persian هر شیء (har šey', “everything”, literally “each thing”), from هر (har, “each, every”) + شیء (“thing, object”), the latter being a borrowing from Arabic شَيْء (šayʔ, “thing”).
From Ottoman Turkish هركس (herkes), from Persian هرکس (harkas), from هر (har, “each, every”) + کس (kas, “person”). See Azerbaijani hər kəs.

parole.significato: khedive, the title of Ottoman viceroy of Egypt from 1805–1914.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish خدیو (hıdiv), from Persian خدیو (xadêw, xedêw, “lord, master, king”).
From Ottoman Turkish حیلهكار (hilekâr), from Persian حیلهگر (hile-gar). Equivalent to hile + -kâr
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خورلامق, from Persian خوار (xvâr). By surface analysis, hor + la-. Cognate with Kazakh қорлау (qorlaw, “to humiliate”).

parole.significato: rooster, cock, chanticleer, an adult male of the species Gallus gallus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خروس (horoz, horos), from Persian خروس (xorus).
From Ottoman Turkish خوریات (horyat), خوریاد (horyad), from Persian خوریاد (xwaryâd), borrowed from Greek χωριάτης (choriátis, “villager”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خوش (hoş), from Persian خوش (xoš).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خونخوار (ḫunḫār), from Persian خونخوار (xunxâr).
From Ottoman Turkish خرده (hurde), from Persian خرده, خورده (xorde).
From Ottoman Turkish خوی (huy), from Persian خو (xu).

parole.significato: A dessert made with saltless fresh cheese, starch and rice flour.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خوشمریم (ḫoşmerim, “a dish of fresh milk milked on sour, (in towns) a dish of cream-cheese stirred over a fire with flour, sugar or honey”) or خوشمرم (ḫoşmerem), from Persian خوش (xoš, “happy, sweet”) + مرم (maram, “clotted cream”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خنكار (hünkâr), from Persian خواندگار (xond-kâr), shortened from Persian خداوندگار (xudâvandgâr, “lord, overlord”).
From Ottoman Turkish خردوات (hurdavat), an Arabic plural form of خرده (hurde), that from Persian خرده.

parole.significato: cucumber, any widely-cultivated vine of the species Cucumis sativus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خیار (hıyar), from Persian خیار (xiyâr, “cucumber”).

parole.significato: golden shower, golden rain tree, any flowering plant of the species Cassia fistula
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خیارشنبه (hıyarşembe), from Persian خیار چنبر (xiyâr čanbar, “golden rain tree”), from خیار (xiyâr, “cucumber”) + چنبر (čanbar, “circle, hoop”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خشم (ḫaşm, ḫışm), from Persian خشم (xašm).

parole.significato: Honorific title given to the Islamic prophet Muhammad.
parole.testo: From Persian انسان کامل (ensân-e kâmel), from Arabic الْإِنْسَان الْكَامِل (al-ʔinsān al-kāmil, literally “the person who has reached perfection”).
From Ottoman Turkish شكمبه (şkembe), from Persian اشکمبه (eškambe) or Persian شکمبه (šekambe).

parole.significato: torture, the infliction of severe pain or anguish, especially as an interrogation technique or punishment
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اشكنجه (işkence, “torture”), from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (şikence, “press”), [script needed] (işkenci, “pain, trouble”), from Persian شکنجه (šekanje, “torment; torture”), اشکنجه (eškanje). Cognate of Azerbaijani işgəncə.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قهوهخانه (kahvehane), from Persian قهوهخانه (qahve-xâne). Equivalent to kahve (“coffee”) + -hane (“house”). Compare Gagauz kafenä, and Azerbaijani qəhvəxana.
From Ottoman Turkish كهیا (kahya), shortening of كتخدا (kethüda), from Persian کدخدا. Doublet of kethüda.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاقم (kakım), from Persian قاقم (qâqom).
From Ottoman Turkish قلاش (kallâš), from Persian قلاش (qallâš), from Arabic قَلَّاش (qallāš), from Persian کلاش (kallâš).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قارنبهار (karnabahar), from Persian کرمب بهار (karamb-i bahâr), from کرمب (karamb) from Ancient Greek κράμβη (krámbē, “cabbage”) + بهار (bahâr, “spring”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاتبقات (ḳat-be-ḳat), from قات (ḳat) and Persian با (bâ).
From Ottoman Turkish قوغا (kavga), from غوغا (gavga), from Persian غوغا (ġowġâ, ġavġâ).

parole.significato: Caesar, title of Roman and Byzantine emperors
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قیصر (kayser), from Persian قیصر (qeysar), ultimately from Latin Caesar. Doublet of çar, Kayseri, and Sezar

parole.significato: a dish made of roast and low-fat cheese placed over chopped bread or yufka
parole.testo: Borrowed from Persian کالهجوش (kâle-juš).

parole.significato: head (of goats and sheep including those of lambs)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كله (kelle), derived from Persian کله (kalle), ultimately from Proto Indo-European *kl̥H- (“bald”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كمانكش, from Persian كمانكش (kamānkash)
From Ottoman Turkish كمانچه (kemançe, kemence), from Persian کمانچه (kamânče).
From Ottoman Turkish كرسته (kereste, “timber; building material”), from Persian كراسته.

parole.significato: caravan (a convoy or procession of travelers, their vehicles and cargo, and any pack animals)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish كروان (kervan), from Persian کاروان (kârvân). Doublet of karavan.
From Ottoman Turkish كاروانسَرای (karvanseray), كَروانسَرای (kervanseray), from Old Anatolian Turkish [Term?], from Persian کاروانسرای (kârvânsarây).
From Ottoman Turkish كیسه (kise, kese), from Persian کیسه (kise).

From Persian تیزاب (têzâb, “nitric acid”) (literally, “sharp/strong water”). Compare Latin aqua fortis with the same literal meaning. The initial “k” is possibly a contamination from Arabic كَذَّاب (kaḏḏāb, “liar”).

parole.significato: drawing (process of drawing or pulling something)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish كشیده (keşide), from Persian کشیده (kešide).
From Ottoman Turkish كشیر (keşir), كشر (keşir), كشور (keşir), from Old Anatolian Turkish كشور (käşür), possibly from Persian گزر (gazar). Compare Turkmen käşir, Azerbaijani keşir.

parole.significato: A traditional Turkish dish similar to Armenian harissa; a sort of meat and wheat or barley stew.
parole.testo: Derived from Ottoman Turkish كشك (keşk), from Persian کشک (kašk).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كیل (kil), from Persian گل (gel).
From Ottoman Turkish كلیم (kilim, “carpet”), from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (kilīm, “blanket”), from Persian گلیم (gelim, “blanket, garment, cloth, carpet”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كلید (ḱilid), from Persian کلید (kelid), from Middle Persian *kilēd, from Ancient Greek κλείς (kleís), from Proto-Hellenic *klāwī́ds, from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂u-.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كین (kin, “a grudge, concealed desire of revenge, malice”),. from Persian كین (kin) or کینه (kine, “hatred, rancor, malevolence”). Doublet of penaltı.
From Ottoman Turkish خمبره (kumbara), from Persian خمباره (xombâra, “an earthenware box, a small jar; a bombshell”).
From Ottoman Turkish قورناز (kurnaz), from Persian قرناس (qornâs).
From Ottoman Turkish كتخدا.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كار (kâr), borrowed from Persian کار (kâr), from Middle Persian [script needed] (kʾl /⁠kār⁠/, “work, deed, affair”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷer- (“to do, make, construct”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كاغد (ḱāğıd) , from Persian کاغذ (kâġaz, “paper”) , from Proto-Common Turkic [Term?] (compare Karakhanid [script needed] (kāɣïd, “paper”)), ultimately from Sogdian 𐼸𐼰𐼲𐼹𐼰 (kʾγδʾ /⁠kāγaδā⁠/); further etymology is unknown, perhaps a borrowing from Old Chinese 紙 (OC *kjeʔ)
From Ottoman Turkish كهنه (ḱöhne), from Persian کهنه (kohne).
From Ottoman Turkish كور (kör), ultimately from Persian کور (kur).

parole.significato: a large kettledrum mostly used in wars
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كوس (kös, küs), from Persian کوس (kôs, “large kettledrum”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كوتی (kötü, köti). Perhaps related to göt (“ass”). For the sense development, compare Arabic دُبْر (dubr, “buttocks->unfortunate”). Initial /k/ preserved unvoiced perhaps to distinguish the word from göt. However, the vowel of the last syllable of kötü cannot be explai

parole.significato: In Ottoman Empire, a handsome young male dancer, cross-dressed in feminine attire, employed as an entertainer.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish كوچك (köçek, “boy dancer; foal”), from Persian کوچک (kuček).

parole.significato: corner, angle; nook; bend (of a road, etc.)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كوشه (köşe), from Persian گوشه (guše).

parole.significato: a piece of paper that is bent into a cone form to put little things inside it
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كلاه (külah), from Persian کلاه (kolâh).

parole.significato: the furnace located in a service room behind the walls, used to heat water which was then delivered to the steam room
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كولخان (külhan, “furnace in a hammam”), itself from Persian گلخان (gulxân, “backroom”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كنبد (kümbed, “dome, cupola”), from Persian گنبد (gonbad).

parole.significato: oil cake, the solid residue remaining after any oilseed has been pressed to remove the vegetable oil
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كوسبه (küsbe, “oil cake”), from Persian کسبه (kusba).
From Ottoman Turkish لاجورد (lâceverd), borrowed from Persian لاجورد (lâjevard). Cognate with Azerbaijani lacivərd, Old Uyghur 𐽾𐽴𐽰𐽱𐽾𐾀 (rzʾvrt /⁠razavart⁠/).

parole.significato: unnecessary or meaningless utterance; empty words
parole.testo: Equivalent to laf + güzaf, ultimately from Persian لاف (lâf) and گزاف (guzaf).
From Ottoman Turkish لكه (“spot, stain, speck”), from Persian لکه.

parole.significato: anchor, a tool used to moor a vessel to the bottom of the sea
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لنگر (lenger), itself from Persian لنگر (langar, “anchor”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لوند (levend), from Persian لوند (lavand, “flirtatious”).
From Ottoman Turkish لكن (leğen), from Persian لگن (lagan), from Ancient Greek λεκάνη (lekánē).
From Ottoman Turkish لشكر (leşker), from Persian لشکر (laškar).

parole.significato: A whey cheese similar to ricotta.
parole.testo: From Persian لور.

parole.significato: the place where tobacco is placed in smoking tools such as hookah, pipe
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لوله, which is from Persian لوله (lūle)

parole.significato: trowel, a plasterer's tool used in spreading and dressing mortar
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ماله (mala), itself from Persian ماله (mâle, “trowel”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مایخوش (mayhoş, “sweet-and-sour”), from Persian مایخوش (mâyxoš), a compound of مایه (mâye, “stuff”) + خوش (xoš, “pleasant”).

parole.significato: sparkler, a hand-held firework that burns slowly while emitting bright sparks
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مایتاب (maytab), from Persian ماهتاب (mâhtâb, “moonlight”).

parole.significato: gall nut, oak apple, oak gall, Aleppo gall
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مازو (mazı, mazu), from Persian مازو (mâzu).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ماشه, from Persian ماشه.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مهتر (mihter, mehter), from Persian مهتر (mehtar).
From Ottoman Turkish مكیك (mekik), from Persian مکوک (makôk).

parole.significato: (of an animal or a plant) Having been bred from two different species; hybrid, half-bred.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ملز (melez, “mixed, half-bred, mongrel”), from Persian ملس (“sweet and sour, twilight, cotton-silk mix fabric, bastard”), from Arabic مَلَس (malas, “twilight”).
From Ottoman Turkish منتشه (menteşe), itself a vulgarization of Persian بندگشا (bandgošâ).

parole.significato: The lentil plant (Lens culinaris), or the seeds of this plant used as food
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مرجمك, from Persian مرجمک (marjomak), vulgarized from مردمك (merdümek) and مردمک (mardomak) respectively. Doublet of mürdümük (“chickling vetch”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مردانه (merdâne, “rolling pin”), from Persian وردانه (vardâne), وردنه (vardane).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مردانه (merdâne, “manly”), from Persian مردانه (mardâne). By surface analysis, mert + -ane.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مرد (merd, “man”), from Persian مرد (mard, “man”), hence the given name.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مزه (meze), from Persian مزه (maze).

parole.significato: Indicates a situation that becomes apparent or is understood later; turns out (that), apparently
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مكر (meğer), from Persian مگر (magar)

parole.significato: A type of cushion or mattress for sitting or lying on.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish مندر (minder), from Persian نیمدار (nimdâr, “outworn but still useful garment”). Cognates include Albanian minder, Bulgarian миндер (minder), Macedonian миндер (minder), Romanian mindir, Serbo-Croatian миндер.
From Ottoman Turkish موم (mum, “candle”), itself from Persian موم (mum).

parole.significato: mummy (embalmed corpse wrapped in linen bandages for burial)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish مومیا (mumıya, mumya), from Persian مومیا (mumiyâ).
From Ottoman Turkish مورد (murd), itself from Persian مورد (murd, “myrtle”).
From Persian مُشته.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مؤذن (müezzin), derived from Persian مؤذن (mo'azzen), derived from Arabic مُؤَذِّن (muʔaḏḏin, “muezzin”).

From Ottoman Turkish مرور (mürver), from Persian مروارید (morvârid, “pearl”), back-formed from expressions like mürver çiçeği, literally pearl flower, and constructions like yer mürveri (“dwarf elder”).

parole.significato: a big nail (spike-shaped metal fastener used for joining wood or similar materials)
parole.testo: Ottoman Turkish میخ (mıh), itself from Persian میخ (mix, “nail”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ناـ (nâ-), from Persian ناـ (nâ-).

parole.significato: hatchet, a small axe with a short handle
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ناجاق (nacak, “poleaxe”), itself from Persian ناچخ (nâčax, “polearm, halberd”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ﻧﺎﺩﻳﺪﻩ, from Persian نادیده (nādīde), compound of prefix ناـ (nâ-) and دیده (dīde). By surface analysis, na- + dide.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نعلبند (nalbant), from Persian نعلبند (na'l-band).
From Ottoman Turkish نام (nam), from Persian نام (nâm), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁nómn̥. Compare Sanskrit नामन् (nāman), Latin nomen, French nom , English name, German Name, Armenian անուն (anun).

parole.significato: person whose marriage is not prohibited by Islamic law
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish ﻧﺎﻣﺤﺮﻡ, from Persian نامحرم (nā-maḥram), compound of prefix ناـ (nâ-) and محرم (maḥram).
From na- (“un-”) + mağlup (“defeated”). The prefix is from Persian ناـ (nâ-).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نامرد, from Persian نامرد (nâmard), compound of prefix ناـ (nâ-) and Persian مرد (mard).
From Ottoman Turkish نامزد (namzed), from Persian نامزد (nâmzad).
By surface analysis, na- + münasip. Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نامناسب which is from Persian نامناسِب (nā-munāsib), compound of prefix ناـ (nâ-) and مناسِب (munāsib).
From Ottoman Turkish نان (nan), from Persian نان (nân).
Ultimately from Persian نان کور (nân kur).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ناتمام (nâtamâm), from Persian ناتمام (nâtamâm), compound of prefix ناـ (nâ-) and تَمَام (tamām). By surface analysis, na- + tamam.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ناز, from Persian ناز (nâz).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نازك (nazik), from Ottoman Turkish نازك (nāzük), from Persian نازک (nâzok, nâzak).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ناچیزانه (nāçizāne), from Persian ناچیزانه (nâčizâne), from ناـ (nâ-, un-, non-, -less) + چیز (čiz, “thing, matter”) + ـانه (-âne, adjective forming suffix).
From Ottoman Turkish نه (ne, “neither; nor”), from Persian نه (na). Cognate to Old English ne (“not”).
From Ottoman Turkish نفت (neft), from Persian نفت (naft).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ناكس, from Persian ناکس (nākas).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نزاكت (nezâket), from Persian نزاکت (nazâkat, nezâkat). Compare Azerbaijani nəzakət.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نیشتر (nişter, “a lancet”) (alternative forms; نشتر (neşter), لشتر (leşter)), from Persian نیشتر (ništar).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نگاهبان (nigâhban), from Persian نگاهبان (negâhbân).
From Ottoman Turkish نيكبين, which is a pseudo-loan from Persian نيك + بین.

From Ottoman Turkish نیلوفر (nîlûfer), from Persian نیلوفر (nilufar), from Middle Persian nylw(k)pl (nīlōpal, “lotus, water-lily”), from Sanskrit नीलोत्पल (nīlotpala, “blue lotus”), from नील (nīla, “blue”) + उत्पल (utpala, “lotus, water-lily”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نیاز (niyaz), from Persian نیاز (niyâz, “need”).
From Ottoman Turkish نشانه, from Persian نشانه.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نشاسته, from Persian نشاسته.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نمونه (numune), from Persian نمونه (nemune).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish رسپی (rospi, rospu, “whore”), اورسپی (orospu), روسپی (ruspi, rospi, rospu), from Persian روسپی (ruspi).
From Ottoman Turkish اویونباز (oyunbaz), from اویون (oyun, “game”) + Persian باز (bâz, “playing”).
From Ottoman Turkish پاپوش, from Persian پاپوش (pâpuš). Related to paça (“hem of a pant leg; trotter”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پاجامه (pacame), from Persian پاجامه (pâjâme, “trousers, drawers”), from پا (pâ, “leg”) + جامه (jâme, “garment”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پادشاه, from Persian پادشاه (pâdšâh, “king, monarch”).
From Ottoman Turkish بها (baha, paha), from Persian بها (bahâ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پاك (pak), from Persian پاک (pâk).

parole.significato: soft saddle with no wooden frame; packsaddle
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish پالان (palan), from Persian پالان (pâlân).
From Ottoman Turkish پاره (pare, para), from Persian پاره (pâre). Doublet of pare.
From Ottoman Turkish پاره پارچه (pare parça), from Persian [Term?]. Equivalent to pare + parça.
From Ottoman Turkish پارچه (parça), from Persian پارچه (pârče), from پاره (pâre) + diminutive suffix چه (če).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پاتلجان (patlıcan), from Persian بادلجان (bâdeljân). Cognate with English aubergine.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پایتخت (payitaht), from Persian پایتخت (pâytaxt).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بازو (bazu, bazı, “upper arm”), from Persian بازو (bâzu, “upper arm”).
From Ottoman Turkish پهلوان (pehlivan), from Persian پهلوان (pahlavân). Perhaps a doublet of balaban (“huge, large; fat”).
From Ottoman Turkish پراكنده (perakende, “dispersed, scattered”), from Persian پراگنده (parâgande).
From Ottoman Turkish پرده (perde), from Persian پرده (parda).
From Ottoman Turkish پرنده (perende), from Persian پرنده.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پری (peri), from Persian پری (pari).
From Ottoman Turkish پریشان (perişan), from Persian پریشان (parêšân).
From Ottoman Turkish پرواسز, from Persian پروا (parvâ), equivalent to perva + -sız.
From Ottoman Turkish پرچین (perçin), from Persian پرچین (parčin, “put together”), پرچین (parčin).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پرشنبه (perşenbe), from older پنجشنبه (pencşenbe), from Persian پنجشنبه (panj-šanbe, “Thursday”), literally "five (days after) Saturday".

parole.significato: Used when accepting defeat; "I yield!" or "Uncle!"
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بس (bes, “Enough! Hold!”, interj.), from Persian بس (bas, “enough”).

parole.significato: That which is sung softly and slowly; bass.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پس (pes, “low and soft or bass voice or tone”), from Persian پست (past, “low, abject”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پس (pes, “the hinder part, back of a thing, pursuit after a thing”), from Persian پس (pas, “back, hind; then, so, therefore”).
From Ottoman Turkish پی (pey, “deposit, bid”), from Persian پی (pey).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پیدا (peydā, “existent, produced, in hand, manifest, visible, born, begotten”), from Persian پیدا (peydâ, “evident, visible, apparent”).

parole.significato: little by little, piece by piece
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پی در پی (pey der pey), from Persian پای (pây, “foot”) and در (dar, “at, in, within”).
From Ottoman Turkish پش (peş), from Persian پس (pas) or پشت (pošt), and possibly influenced by پیش (piš, “front”).
From Ottoman Turkish پشین (peşin), from Persian پیشین (pišin, “previous”).
From Ottoman Turkish پیشكش, from Persian پیشکش.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پیشگیر (peşgir, peşkir), from Persian پیشگیر (pêš-gir).
From Persian پیر (pir).
From Ottoman Turkish پیراهن (pirahen), itself from Persian پیراهن (pirâhan, “shirt”).
Probably from Persian پیس (“stained, wrinkled, leprous”) (archaic), whence also Azerbaijani pis (“bad, dirty”), Northern Kurdish pîs (“dirty”) and Armenian փիս (pʻis).
From Ottoman Turkish پیاده, from Persian پیاده.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پوته, from Persian بوته.
From Ottoman Turkish پول (“small disc; scale; wafer, stamp”), possibly from Persian پول (pul, “coin”) and Ancient Greek ὀβολός (obolós).

parole.significato: idol (object or thing of spiritual worship)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بت (but) (also vulgar پوت (put)), from Persian بت (“idol”), from Middle Persian bwt' (“Buddha, idol”), ultimately from Sanskrit बुद्ध (buddha).
From Ottoman Turkish پوشت (puşt), from Persian پشت (pošt, “rear, back”).
From Ottoman Turkish پر (pür, “full; abundant; numerous; frequent”), from Persian پر (por).
From Ottoman Turkish پختی (pıhtı), from Persian پختی (“jelly”).

parole.significato: to encounter, to meet by chance
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish راستلامق (rastlamak), verb formed from راست (rast, “luck, success; encounter, meeting”), a semantic evolution of Persian راست (râst).
From Ottoman Turkish رهبر (rehber), from Persian رهبر (rahbar).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish رنگارنك (rengârenk), from Persian رنگارنگ (rangârang, “colorful”).
From Ottoman Turkish روا, ultimately from Persian روا.

parole.significato: basbousa, a traditional Ottoman semolina cake topped with syrup
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish روغنی (revğani, “oily, syrupy”), from Persian روغن (rowġan, “oil, butter”).
From Ottoman Turkish ریاكار (riyakar), from Persian ریاکار (riyâkâr). Equivalent to riya + -kâr.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish روزنامه (ruznâme), from Persian روزنامه (ruznâme, “newspaper; diary”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish روزكار (rüzgâr, “wind”), from Persian روزگار (ruzgâr).
From Persian ریخ.
From Ottoman Turkish ساخته (sahte), from Persian ساخته (sâxte).

parole.significato: morocco, saffian, a soft leather made from goatskins or sheepskins which is later tanned and dyed
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سختیان (sahtiyan, “dyed goatskin”), from Persian [Term?].
From Ottoman Turkish صمیمی (samimi), from Persian صمیمی (samimi), or formed like it in Ottoman Turkish from Arabic صَمِيم (ṣamīm, “marrow, core”).
From Ottoman Turkish سمور (samur), from Persian سمور (samur); see there for more.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صندلیه (sandaliyye), from Persian صندلی (sandali).
From Ottoman Turkish سرای (seray, saray), borrowed from Persian سرای (sarây).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سایه (saye), from Persian سایه (sâye, “shadow, shade”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ساز (sāz, “a stringed musical instrument”), from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (sāz, “musical instrument”), from Persian ساز (sâz).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish سدف (sedef), from Persian سداب (sadâb).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سفربر (seferber), from Persian سفربر (safarbar, “who undertakes a journey, ready to travel”).

parole.significato: tripod, a three-legged stand, mount, or stool
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سهپا (sehpâ), from Persian سهپا (se-pâ), a compound of سه (se, “three”) + پا (pâ, “leg”).
From Ottoman Turkish سپت, itself from Persian سبد (sabad, “basket”).
From Ottoman Turkish سربست (serbest), from Persian سربست (sarbast).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سردار (serdâr), from Persian سردار (sardâr). By surface analysis, ser + -dar.

parole.significato: a leader of bandits or irregulars
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سركرده (sergerde, serkerde), from Persian سرکرده (sarkarde).
From Ottoman Turkish سركذشت (sergüzeşt), from Persian سرگذشت (sargozašt), from سر (sar) and گذاشتن (gozâštan).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سرمایه (sermaye), from Persian سرمایه (sarmâye).
From Ottoman Turkish سرسم (sersem), from Persian سرسام (sarsâm, “brain inflamation, brain tumor”), combination of Persian سر (sar, “head”) and Persian سام (sâm, “fever”).
From Ottoman Turkish سرسری (serseri, “whimsical, vagrant, vagabond”) from Persian سرسری (sarsari).
From Ottoman Turkish سرت, from Persian سرد (sard, “cool; unkind”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سرور, from Persian سَروَر (sarvar).
From Ottoman Turkish سروی (servi), from Persian سرو (sarv), from Middle Persian 𐫘𐫡𐫇 (srw /⁠sarw⁠/, “cypress”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سیمین, from Persian سیمین (sīmīn, “silver”)

parole.significato: A bagel or ring doughnut shaped bread roll covered with sesame seeds.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish سمید (simit), from Persian سمید (semid, “semolina”), from Arabic سَمِيد (samīd, “semolina”), from Aramaic סְמִידָא / ܣܡܻܝܕܳܐ (səmīḏā), from Akkadian 𒆠𒅔𒆠𒅔𒄯𒄯 (/⁠samīdu⁠/, “a type of fine groats, coarse flour, semolina”), related to Akkadian 𒀀𒊏𒄯𒄯 (/⁠samādu⁠/, “to grind fine”).
From Ottoman Turkish سنجاب (sincab), from Persian سنجاب (sanjâb). Replaced the native word teyin, still in use in dialects.
From Ottoman Turkish سینه (sîne), from Persian سینه (sîne).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سپر (siper), from Persian سپر (separ, “shield”).
From Ottoman Turkish ستم (sitem, “injury, malice; scolding, reprimand”), from Persian ستم (setam).
From Ottoman Turkish سیاه (siyah), from Persian سیاه (siyâh).
From Ottoman Turkish سفره, صوفره (sofra), from Persian سفره (sofre) from Arabic سُفْرَة (sufra).
From Ottoman Turkish صوفته, from Persian سوخته.
From Ottoman Turkish سوقاق, from Persian زقاق, from Arabic زُقَاق (zuqāq).
From Persian ﺳﻮﺩﻩ (sude).
From Ottoman Turkish سواری (süvari), alteration of Persian سوار (sovâr, “rider, cavalryman”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طاقت (takat), from Persian طاقت (tâqat), from Arabic طَاقَة (ṭāqa).
From Ottoman Turkish دانه (tane), from Persian دانه (dâne).
From Ottoman Turkish طرفدار (tarafdar), from Persian طرفدار (tarafdâr), from Arabic طَرَف (ṭaraf, “side”) + Persian ـدار (-dâr). By surface analysis, taraf + -dar.

parole.significato: A dried food based on a fermented mixture of grain and yogurt or fermented milk, usually made into a thick soup with wa…
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تارخانه (tarhana), from Persian ترخوانه (tarxvâne), compound of تر (tar, “moist”) and خوان (xvân, “table”).
From Ottoman Turkish تاوه (tâva), from Persian تاوه (tâve).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تازه (tâze), from Persian تازه (tâze).

parole.significato: To replace with a new or fresh one; to refresh, to replenish.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تازهلمك (tāzelemek, “to renew, to freshen up, to replenish”), from Ottoman Turkish تازه (tāze, “fresh, new, young and tender, raw, inexperienced”), from Persian تازه (tâze, “fresh, new”). By surface analysis, taze + -le + -mek.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تازی (tazı), from Persian تازی (tâzi)
From Persian تهدید (tahdid), from Arabic تَهْدِيد (tahdīd).
From Ottoman Turkish تنبل (tenbel), from Persian تنبل (tanbal).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تن (ten), from Persian تن (tan).
From Ottoman Turkish تنكه, from Persian تنگه, from Persian تنک (tonok, “تنک”, literally “thin”), from Proto-Indo-European *ténh₂us (“thin”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تنها (tenha), from Persian تنها (tanhâ).
From Ottoman Turkish ترازو (terazu, terazi), from Persian ترازو (tarâzu).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ترجمه حال (tercüme-i hâl), from Persian ترجمه حال (tarjome-ye hâl).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ترهیاغی (tere yağı), some sources claim it is derived from Persian کره (kare, “butter”) (compare Azerbaijani kərə yağı), however others dispute the consonant shift from /k/ to /t/ as impossible, and claim the origin to be Persian تر (ter, “humid, wet; fresh”), indicati
From Ottoman Turkish ترزی (terzi), from Persian درزی (darzi).
From Persian تازیانه (tâziyâne, “scourge, lash, whip”).
From Ottoman Turkish تزكاه (tezgâh), from Persian دستگاه (dastgâh).

From Ottoman Turkish تفتیك, تفتك (tiftik), دفتك (diftik), from Persian تفتیک (taftik), also تفدیگ (tafdig). Akin to Azerbaijani tiftik, Armeno-Kipchak դիֆդիգ (tiftik), դիվդիգ (tivtik). Nişanyan traces the word to the form II verbal noun of Arabic ف ت ك (f t k) related to slaughtering, but the spelli

parole.significato: A dish made by adding fried or stale bread into gravy.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تریت (terit, tirit, “a sop of bread, moistened with gravy and stewed”), shares common origin with Persian ترید (tarid, “bread moistened with milk or water”), from Arabic ثَرِيد (ṯarīd, “dish of bread in broth”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تیز (tiz), from Persian تیز (tiz).
From Ottoman Turkish تخم (tuhm, tohum), from Persian تخم (toxm), from Proto-Indo-European *tewk- (“germ, seed, sprout, offspring”).
From Ottoman Turkish دلبند (dülbend), from Persian دلبند (dolband). Doublet of türban.

parole.significato: timar, a kind of Ottoman Empire fief granted by the Sultan to a spahi in exchange for his cavalryman service and cultiv…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تیمار (timar, “timar, an Ottoman fief”), from Persian تیمار (timâr, “care, nurture”).
From Ottoman Turkish تراش (tıraş, traş), from Persian تراش (tarâš). Distantly related to teknoloji (“technology”) and tekstil (“textile”) through Proto-Indo-European.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوستره (ustura), from Persian استره (ostore, “razor”).
From Ottoman Turkish وای (vay), from Persian وای (vây, “alas!”), from Proto-Indo-European *wai. Cognate with English woe, Latin vae, Lithuanian vai̇̃, Russian увы́ (uvý), Old Irish fae, among others.

parole.significato: to abandon, give up, let up, stop doing something, not do something (+ ablative)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish واز گچمك (vaz geçmek). Partial calque of Persian باز آمدن (bâz âmadan). Cognate with Kazakh баз кешу (baz kešüw).
From Ottoman Turkish ویران (viran), Old Anatolian Turkish ویران (vīrān), itself from Persian ویران (virân, “ruined, devasted”). Doublet of ören.
From Ottoman Turkish یابان, from Persian یابان (yâbân).

parole.significato: related to the wilderness or outdoors
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish یابانی, an adjective form of Persian یابان (yâbân).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish یادگار (yâdigâr), from Persian یادگار.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish یاور (yâver), from Persian یاور (yâvar).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish یك (yek, “one”), from Persian یک (yek).
From Ottoman Turkish یكپاره (yekpare), from Persian یک پاره (yak-pâre, “one-piece”).

parole.significato: Greek, relating to Greece or Greeks.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish یونان (Yunan), from Old Anatolian Turkish یونان (Yunan), from Persian یونان (yunân), from Old Persian 𐎹𐎢𐎴 (yauna, “Ionia”), from Ancient Greek Ἰᾱ́ων (Iā́ōn, “Ionian”), of uncertain origin.
From Ottoman Turkish یاد (yâd, “remembrance”), from Persian یاد (yâd).
From Ottoman Turkish یار (yâr, “friend, a beloved friend, one's lover”), from Persian یار (yâr).
From Ottoman Turkish زاده (zade), from Persian زاده (zâde), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁-.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زمپاره (zampara) or زنباره (zenpāre), from Persian زنباره (zan-bâre).
From Ottoman Turkish زبون (zebun), from Persian زبون (zabun).
From Ottoman Turkish زهر (zehr, zehir), from Persian زهر (zahr).

parole.significato: coil spring, a mechanical device made of flexible or coiled material
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زنبرك (zenberek, “crossbow; spring”), itself from Persian زنبورک (zanburak).

parole.significato: ginger, any flowering plant of the species Zingiber officinale
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زنجفیل (zencefil), from Classical Persian زنجفیل (zanjafīl), from Arabic زَنْجَبِيل (zanjabīl), from Classical Syriac ܙܢܓܒܝܠ (zangabīl), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀲𑀺𑀁𑀕𑀺𑀯𑁂𑀭 (siṃgivera), ultimately from Old Tamil 𑀇𑀜𑁆𑀘𑀺𑀯𑁂𑀭𑁆 (iñcivēr).
From Ottoman Turkish زردالو (zerdalu, zerdali), from Old Anatolian Turkish زردالو (zerdalu), from Persian زردآلو (zard-âlu).
From Ottoman Turkish زبیدی (zibidi), from an unattested Persian word akin to زیبیدن (zibidan).
From Ottoman Turkish زل (zil), perhaps from Persian زیر (zir).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زیان (ziyān, “harm, injury, loss”), from Persian زیان.
From Ottoman Turkish زور, from Persian زور (zor).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زوربه (zorba, “rebel, extorter”), from Persian زور (zor, “force, violence”).
From Ottoman Turkish زورلو, زورلی (zorlu), equivalent to zor + -lu. Although -lu is attached to nouns and zor is an adjective, it was originally a noun when it was borrowed from Persian زور (zur).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زورنا (zurnâ), itself from Persian سرنا (sornâ).
From Ottoman Turkish زمرد (zümrüd), from Persian زمرد (zomorrod), from Ancient Greek σμάραγδος (smáragdos).
From Ottoman Turkish زره (zırıh, zırh), from Persian زره (zere).
Ultimately from Persian زلو با (zirbā)

parole.significato: laundry (that which needs to be laundered)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چاماشیر (çamaşır), from combination of Persian جامه (jâme) and Persian شور (šur), present stem of Persian شستن (šostan).
From Ottoman Turkish چانطه (çanta, “leather bag, small suitcase”), from Persian چنته.
From Ottoman Turkish چاپراز (çapraz), from Persian چپ راست (“left–right”).

parole.significato: A wheel-shaped piece of machinery, like a cogwheel or a gear.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چرخ (çark, “wheel; machine”), from Persian چرخ (čarx), from Middle Persian 𐫝𐫍𐫡 (chr /⁠čahr⁠/, “wheel, cycle”), from Proto-Iranian *čaxrám, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čakrám, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷékʷlos (“wheel, circle”). Doublet of çakra.

parole.significato: cross, torture stake; cruciform mechanism used for torturing
parole.testo: From Persian چارمیخ (čârmix).
From Persian چادر شب (čâdar-e šab).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چهارشنبه (çarşanba, çehârşenbe), from Persian چهارشنبه (čahâr-šanbe, “Wednesday”, literally “four (days after) Saturday”).
From Ottoman Turkish چارشی (çarşı), چارشو (çarşu, “marketplace”), from older چارسو (çarsu, “street of shops”), from Persian چارسو (“crossroads”), from چار (“four”) + سو (su, “direction”).
From Ottoman Turkish چای (çay), from Persian چای (čây), from Sinitic 茶 (chá).
From Ottoman Turkish چایدانلق (çaydanlık), from Persian چایدان (čâydân) + -lık.

parole.significato: a belled daf or finger cymbals
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چاغنه (çağana), from Persian چغانه (çeğâne).

parole.significato: unripe nut of several stone fruits, especially an unripe almond
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چاغلا (çağla, “unripe almond”), which derives from Persian چغاله (čaġâle, “unripe fruit”).

From Persian چهره, from Middle Persian 𐭰𐭧𐭫𐭪𐭩 (čihrag), from Old Persian *čiθrakah, from Proto-Iranian *čiθrákah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čitrás, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷi-tróm, from *kʷey- (“bright, burning”).

parole.significato: hook, a rod bent in curved shape
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چنگل (çengel, “hook”), itself from Persian چنگال (čangâl, “fork; hook; claw”).

parole.significato: a type of harp formerly common in the Ottoman Empire
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چنك (çeng), from Persian چنگ.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چراغ (çerağ), from Persian چراغ (čerâġ). Doublet of çıra and çırak.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چرز (çerez, “hors d'oeuvres, appetizer, snack”), from Persian چرس. Also compare Ottoman Turkish چرس. Unrelated to Azerbaijani çerez above.
From Persian جهیز (jehiz). Doublet of cihaz.
From Ottoman Turkish چشمه (çeşme), from Persian چشمه.
From Ottoman Turkish چفت (çift), from Persian جفت (joft).

parole.significato: a kick with two legs (often for odd-toed ungulates)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چفته (çifte), from Persian جفته (jofte), with some separate Ottoman developments from چفت (çift).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چله (çille, çile), from Old Anatolian Turkish چلّه (çille), from Persian چلّه (čilla). Cognate with Azerbaijani çilə.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جله (cülle), from Persian جله.
From Ottoman Turkish چلنكیر (çilingir), from چلانكر (cilanger), from Persian چلنگر (čelengar).

parole.significato: The letter چ of the Persian and Ottoman Turkish alphabets.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چیم (çim), from Persian [Term?].
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چینی (çini), from Persian چینی (čini).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چراغ (çirağ), from Persian چراغ (čerâġ, čarâġ).

From Ottoman Turkish چوبان (çoban), from Middle Turkic ‘çupan’, Proto-Bulgar ‘çoban’. Loaned into Proto-Mongolian *čolbun "Venus". From Ottoman Turkish چوراب (çorap, çorab), from Persian جوراب (jôrâb).

parole.significato: A rough fabric generally woven of animal hair.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چول (çul, “haircloth, a horse's covering or blanket, a horse-cloth”), from Persian جل (joll) or جول (jūl, “horse-covering, saddlecloth”), shares common origin with Arabic جُلّ (jull, “horse-covering, saddlecloth”). Cognate with Azerbaijani çul, Turkmen jul, Uyghur جۇل
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوال (çuval), from Persian جوال (juvâl, “sack”).
Perhaps from Persian چوبک.
From Ottoman Turkish چونكه (çünki, “because”), from Persian چون (čun) + که (ke).
From Ottoman Turkish چرا, from Persian چراغ (čerâġ). Doublet of çırak and çerağ
From Ottoman Turkish چراغ (çerag, çirag), چراق (çırak, “lamp, lantern; light; wick, candlewick; illuminator; teacher, mentor”), from Persian چراغ (čerâġ, čarâġ). Doublet of çerağ and çıra.
From Ottoman Turkish شاد (şâd), from Persian شاد (šâd).
From Ottoman Turkish شاكرد (şakird), شاگرد (şagird), from Persian شاگرد (šâgerd). Compare Armenian աշակերտ (ašakert), Azerbaijani şagird.
From Ottoman Turkish شال, borrowed from Persian شال (šâl).
From Ottoman Turkish شالوار (şalvar), from Persian شلوار (šalvâr).
From Ottoman Turkish شمعدان (şemʼdan), from Persian شمعدان (šam'dân), compound of the Arabic شَمْع (šamʕ) + Persian ـدان (-dân).
From Ottoman Turkish شایان, from Persian شایان.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شاهزاده, from Persian شاهزاده (šāhzāda). By surface analysis, şah + zade.

From Ottoman Turkish شكر (şeker), from Classical Persian شکر (šakar), from Sanskrit शर्करा (śárkarā, “ground or candied sugar", originally "grit, gravel”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱorkeh₂ (“gravel, boulder”). Compare English sugar. Doublet of sakkaroz.
From Persian شکرپاره (šakarpâre).
From Persian شمشیر (šamšir).

parole.significato: a slope in a fortification, an escarp or counterscarp
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish شیو (şiv, şev), from Persian شیب (šib).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شش (şeş), from Persian شش (šeš).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شكار (şikâr), from Persian شکار (šekâr, “hunt”)
From Ottoman Turkish شیوه (şive), from Persian شیوه (šive).

parole.significato: shirdan (the abomasum (fourth and final stomach of a ruminant) eaten as food)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شیردان (şirdan, “a vessel for holding milk, the second stomach of ruminants”), from Persian شیردان, from شیر (šīr, “milk”) + ـدان (-dân, “holder, container”).

parole.significato: to get excited, enthusiastic, become exuberant, become ebullient
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish جوشمق (cōşmak, “to boil up, overflow, become lively”), earliest attestation is from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (cōş, “boil”), ultimately from Proto-Common Turkic *čōš-. Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لالا (lâlâ), لله (lala), from Persian لله (lala /lale) or from Persian لالا (lālā /lâlâ).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دستكاهدار (destgâhdar, tezgâhdar, “a shopman, an assistant who helps customers”) (alternatively تزكاهدار (tezgâhtar)), from Persian دستگاه (dastgâh) and دار, equivalent to tezgâh + -tar.
From Persian وشق (vašaq) or from Proto-Turkic [Term?].

parole.significato: what if (used to introduce speculation about future)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish یا (ya), from Persian یا (yâ, “either, or”).
